priorities.summary: A stack-based buffer overflow in the DIR-600L's authentication.cgi lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary code by manipulating the id and password parameters; the exploit is now public. Affects firmware 2.17 / 2.17b02 — disconnect or replace affected routers, as no vendor fix is listed.
priorities.plain: D-Link DIR-600L routers let a remote attacker run code on the device without logging in; disconnect or replace affected routers.

priorities.summary: An out-of-bounds write in the TEW-657BRM's mini_httpd setup.cgi can be triggered remotely without authentication, and the exploit has been disclosed publicly. TRENDnet says the router has been end-of-life for over 15 years, so no patch is expected — replace the device.
priorities.plain: TRENDnet TEW-657BRM routers let a remote attacker crash or take over the device; the model is long out of support, so replace it.

priorities.summary: Improper output encoding in the JSON-RPC API of FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer lets an unauthenticated attacker execute unauthorized code via a specially crafted HTTP request. Fortinet's November patch batch fixes it — upgrade FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer 8.0.x and 7.6.x.
priorities.plain: FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer let an attacker without a login run commands on the system; apply Fortinet's November patches now.

model.name: Qwen4-Max Preview
model.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team opened a two-week preview of Qwen4-Max, the first model of its next-generation Qwen4 family, on November 11 — a flagship multimodal model for coding, office work and complex agent tasks, available through the Token Plan subscription and Alibaba's own apps. The preview runs until November 25, when the model is retired, and no benchmarks or weights have been published yet.
model.plain: Alibaba's next flagship model is available to test for two weeks — useful for clients weighing Chinese frontier models for coding and agent work.
